evidence.exact_quote: - The executor does not recreate missing directories when a removed worktree makes the original path unavailable.

items.impact: A path can disappear, be rebound, or become a symlink between resolution and mutation or revert; without atomic path identity checks, the non-recreation rule does not prevent mutation of the wrong target.
items.statement: EP-091 specifies removed-worktree failure behavior but does not define race-safe path validation, symlink handling, or an atomic identity check spanning resolution and mutation.
items.title: Worktree path races remain unspecified

evidence.exact_quote: - execution_unit_context must not persist secrets, tokens, passwords, credentials, API keys, provider auth values, or local machine secrets.

items.impact: Producers can disagree about redaction timing, derived sensitive values, retention, replay eligibility, and deletion, causing privacy and cross-document conformance failures despite the no-secret rule.
items.statement: EP-092 closes field ownership and forbids secret persistence, but the excerpt does not provide executable redaction, retention, deletion, or replay oracles for the context lifecycle.
items.title: Execution context privacy lifecycle lacks oracles

evidence.exact_quote: - effective account, execution role, and blocked-episode approval scope survive execution handoff.

items.impact: A handoff can continue under revoked, expired, or superseded authority unless freshness and revalidation semantics are canonical.
items.statement: Permission carry-through is explicit, but revocation, expiry, scope narrowing, account removal, and revalidation during or after handoff are unspecified.
items.title: Carried authority has no revocation transition

evidence.exact_quote: - Ask mode reads context from worktree files.

items.impact: Modes may diverge when the bound worktree is missing, unreadable, stale, conflicted, or remotely unavailable, producing inconsistent user and executor behavior.
items.statement: The happy-path mode matrix is explicit, but the matrix has no defined failure behavior or oracle for unavailable or invalid worktree context.
items.title: Mode matrix omits worktree failure states

evidence.exact_quote: - Mode transitions do not change the active worktree binding.

items.impact: Concurrent mode changes, thread rebinding, and worktree removal can violate the invariant or execute against a stale binding without a defined conflict outcome.
items.statement: EP-095 states the thread-level invariant but does not define atomicity, versioning, or conflict handling when binding state changes concurrently with a mode transition.
items.title: Thread binding transition atomicity is undefined

evidence.exact_quote: - The retired bridge does not create WorkNodes, NodeSeeds, executable queues, final node manifests, or production build tasks.

items.impact: The unit cannot be mistaken for runtime enablement or product coverage and preserves atomized ownership boundaries.
items.statement: EP-001 explicitly retires the bridge and forbids executable artifact creation, closing the migration-lineage authority ambiguity.
items.title: Retired bridge boundary is explicit

evidence.exact_quote: - Section 5 is restored or explicitly aliased as a structural parent without changing scheduler behavior.

items.impact: A restored section and an alias can produce different anchors, consumer resolution, and precedence, leaving cross-document callers dependent on implementation choice.
items.statement: EP-096 permits either restoration or aliasing of Section 5 without specifying the canonical option, anchor behavior, or compatibility mapping.
items.title: Section 5 recovery has two unresolved forms

evidence.exact_quote: - Executor runtime recovery behavior is read through named owner sections and PlanUnits rather than additive addendum order.

items.impact: Implementers have a direct rule that prevents historical addendum order from becoming an accidental precedence layer.
items.statement: EP-097 explicitly subordinates historical addenda to named owner sections and PlanUnits.
items.title: Runtime addendum precedence is closed

evidence.exact_quote: - Executor scheduler readiness, blocked/backoff, retry, capacity, wakeup, and failure-class semantics remain canonical for WorkNodes.

items.impact: Different capacity accounting or fairness choices can starve lanes, oversubscribe providers, or reorder runnable work while still claiming conformance.
items.statement: Scheduler ownership is clear, but capacity units, reservation/release rules, fairness, starvation bounds, and overload observability are not defined.
items.title: Capacity-aware dispatch lacks a capacity model

evidence.exact_quote: - ExecutorIntakeReport validates graph integrity, source-control/test/model/authority metadata, readiness prerequisites, and scheduler metadata.

items.impact: Retries or crashes can duplicate acceptance, expose contradictory accepted/blocked reports, or dispatch against a superseded request revision.
items.statement: Executor intake has validation categories and outcomes but no idempotency key, request revision binding, atomic commit point, or crash-recovery rule.
items.title: Executor intake has no transactional identity

evidence.exact_quote: - Mutation-capable WorkNodes have repo/worktree/baseline/safe-point context before risky execution.

items.impact: Repository, branch, worktree, permission, or model state can change after preflight and before mutation, invalidating rollback and safety assumptions.
items.statement: EP-100 records rich preflight state but does not specify a lock, compare-and-swap, freshness token, or mandatory recheck at mutation time.
items.title: Preflight state can become stale before mutation

evidence.exact_quote: - Manual-only acceptance is not sufficient for WorkNode completion.

items.impact: GUI, accessibility, localization, emulator, and device work can be blocked indefinitely or accepted under inconsistent override behavior because required automated oracles and override authority are unspecified.
items.statement: The no-manual-only rule is strong, but the required oracle by test class, unavailable-harness recovery contract, and any override authority or audit trail are not closed.
items.title: Automated verification fallback is under-specified

evidence.exact_quote: - Failure signatures are normalized and counted across repair attempts.

items.impact: Different normalization and threshold choices can cause infinite repair loops, premature escalation, or counter races across concurrent attempts.
items.statement: Failure-signature counting and escalation stages are named, but normalization equivalence, attempt budgets, time windows, concurrency behavior, and transition thresholds are not specified.
items.title: Repair loop breakers lack deterministic thresholds

evidence.exact_quote: - Every Executor handoff has artifact, owner, validator, receipt, retry, rollback, and escalation fields.

items.impact: Partial or reordered receipt writes can yield false completion, orphaned effects, or tampered chains without a canonical linkage and atomicity model.
items.statement: EP-103 enumerates receipts and fields but does not define immutable chain linkage, ordering, signatures or hashes, idempotency, partial-write recovery, or finalization atomicity.
items.title: Receipt chain integrity is not executable

evidence.exact_quote: - Do not start a partially accepted required WorkGraph.

items.impact: A crash or concurrent graph revision can leave some requests provisioned or activated despite the all-required acceptance invariant.
items.statement: The all-required activation rule is explicit, but its transaction boundary, rollback of provisioning side effects, crash recovery, and graph revision compare are not defined.
items.title: All-required activation lacks atomic commit semantics

evidence.exact_quote: - Discovery output cannot satisfy verifier pass criteria without exact verification.

items.impact: Ranked discovery candidates cannot be promoted into edit or verification authority without exact evidence.
items.statement: EP-106 clearly limits discovery to orientation and requires exact evidence for verifier pass.
items.title: Discovery evidence boundary is explicit

evidence.exact_quote: - clean-room fixture

items.impact: The same fixture scenarios can pass under incompatible interpretations of atomicity, cancellation, restart, and incomplete-content detection.
items.statement: EP-105 demands a broad clean-room fixture suite but does not define fixture inputs, deterministic expected receipts and states, failure injection points, or pass/fail oracle per scenario.
items.title: Clean-room fixture lacks deterministic case oracles

evidence.exact_quote: - Attempt limit counts the initial selected/requested model plus every automatic switch attempt.

items.impact: Conflicting global and section limits or repeated partial failures can produce inconsistent stop behavior and budget consumption.
items.statement: Attempt counting is defined, but precedence between configurable global and section limits, zero or invalid values, budget exhaustion, and concurrent update snapshots is not.
items.title: Fallback bounds lack precedence and edge semantics

evidence.exact_quote: - Unsafe upstream runtime behavior produces blocked/quarantined evidence rather than execution.

items.impact: A compromised or stale validation artifact could be activated, and quarantined behavior could be released without a canonical authority or fresh validation.
items.statement: The PM-owned validation boundary is strong, but artifact authenticity, expiry, activation atomicity, quarantine release authority, rollback triggers, and rollback-failure handling are unspecified.
items.title: Runtime adapter trust and quarantine lifecycle is incomplete

evidence.exact_quote: - Every host action is accepted or blocked through Executor intake, preflight, authority checks, and expected receipts.

items.impact: Broad host commands can leak credentials, overreach filesystem or network scope, leave partial side effects, or retain sensitive transcripts despite passing intake.
items.statement: EP-109 lists intake policies but does not define enforceable command sandbox boundaries, secret injection and revocation, transcript redaction, cleanup verification, or recovery from partial host effects.
items.title: Host action intake lacks enforceable sandbox semantics

evidence.exact_quote: - Cumulative snapshots are persisted once

items.impact: Reconnects, duplicate delivery, process crashes, or concurrent writers can still persist duplicates or omit the terminal turn without a stable admission identity and transaction boundary.
items.statement: EP-110 states once-only persistence but does not define the idempotency key, snapshot replacement rule, atomic durable write, restart reconstruction, or duplicate-delivery oracle.
items.title: Once-only history persistence is not operationalized

evidence.exact_quote: - Transport decision receipts include locality, auth, replay, backpressure, fallback, and provider support

items.impact: Adapters can choose different transports or insecure fallback paths from the same facts while emitting superficially complete receipts.
items.statement: Receipt dimensions are named, but transport eligibility, preference order, auth downgrade prohibition, fallback transition rules, and replay compatibility checks are not defined.
items.title: Transport receipts do not define selection policy

evidence.exact_quote: - UI distinguishes provider stall, WS reconnect, backend stall, and UI render lag.

items.impact: Users can receive misleading diagnoses or inaccessible status if classification evidence, state precedence, recovery actions, announcements, and localized labels are left to implementation.
items.statement: EP-112 names four UI diagnostics but does not define their observable classifiers, simultaneous-state precedence, recovery actions, accessibility semantics, localization contract, or false-classification oracle.
items.title: Backpressure diagnostics lack GUI state semantics

evidence.exact_quote: - Provider native item IDs are kept only where allowed by replay policy.

items.impact: Provider identifiers may be retained, replayed, or deleted inconsistently across adapters, exposing privacy data or breaking deduplication and migration.
items.statement: EP-113 depends on an allowed replay policy but does not name its owner, closed decision inputs, per-provider retention and deletion rules, or compatibility behavior for unknown provider item types.
items.title: Provider replay policy is an unresolved seam

evidence.exact_quote: - Missing terminal stream events time out after 5000 ms as retryable provider_transient inactivity_timeout rather than durable assistant content.

items.impact: Implementers and tests have a deterministic timeout, classification, and durable-history exclusion oracle.
items.statement: EP-114 closes key scheduler and transport values with exact wake ordering, timeout, backpressure, and receipt behavior.
items.title: FABLE runtime constants are explicit

evidence.exact_quote: Conditional requirements: `plan_unit` requires `unit_id` and `owner_doc_refs[]`; `tool_attempt` requires `tool_call_id`, `permission_snapshot_id`, and `attempt_id`; `verification` requires `validator_id`, `target_ref`, and `evidence_ref`; `repair_slice` requires `audit_id`, `finding_key`, and `owner_doc_refs[]`.

items.impact: Execution-unit variants have a direct, falsifiable required-field matrix rather than implicit builder inference.
items.statement: The segment's execution_unit_context addendum gives explicit conditional required fields for four execution-unit types.
items.title: Execution-unit conditional requirements are concrete

evidence.exact_quote: If sub-counters disagree with `attempt_count`, the executor records `attempt_counter_mismatch` with `attempt_id`, `attempt_count`, `subcounter_name`, `subcounter_value`, `expected_value`, and `recovery_action`. `recovery_action` values are `recompute_from_events`, `block_for_manual_repair`, and `ignore_non_authoritative_projection`. Event history is authoritative; projections must be recomputed before any retry/skip/complete transition.

items.impact: Implementations can choose incompatible recovery actions for the same mismatch, potentially ignoring a projection that is actually safety-relevant or blocking indefinitely.
items.statement: The mismatch record and recovery action enum are closed, but the decision authority and deterministic predicate selecting each recovery action are not specified.
items.title: Attempt-counter recovery choice lacks a decision rule

evidence.exact_quote: Dedup identity is `event_name + node_id + attempt_id + event_sequence`. Timestamp is metadata only. If `event_sequence` is missing in imported source, the migration reader derives `event_sequence` from stable event-stream order and records `dedup_sequence_derived = true`. New executor events must carry monotonic `event_sequence` per attempt.

items.impact: Different readers can derive different sequences from partially ordered, duplicated, or concurrently merged imports, defeating deduplication and replay consistency.
items.statement: The dedup tuple is explicit, but stable event-stream order, tie handling, collision detection, and recovery for malformed or merged imported streams are not defined.
items.title: Derived event sequence lacks a stable ordering algorithm

segments.summary: Reviewed worktree resolution, execution context, permission carry-through, mode routing, thread binding, and retired migration lineage. Exact behavior is present, while race safety, authority freshness, privacy lifecycle, and failure matrices remain materially open.

Reviewed runtime owner recovery, addendum precedence, WorkNode scheduling and intake, source-control and model preflight, automated test binding, and repair loop breaking. Precedence is closed; transactional intake, capacity, TOCTOU safety, verification fallback, and loop thresholds are not.

Reviewed execution receipts, three-stage activation, discovery evidence, WorkNodeRecord materialization and fixtures, bounded model fallback, and PM-owned adapter activation. Exact evidence boundaries are strong; receipt integrity, atomic activation, fixture oracles, fallback precedence, and adapter trust lifecycle remain open.

Reviewed host capability intake, durable stream history, transport selection receipts, backpressure diagnostics, and replay admission. The major gaps are enforceable host sandboxing, once-only persistence semantics, transport decision policy, accessible GUI failure states, and replay-policy ownership.

Reviewed deterministic wake coalescing, score ordering, stream timeout and backpressure constants, transport receipts, conditional execution-context requirements, counter mismatch recovery, and event dedup sequencing. Constants and field matrices are concrete; recovery selection and imported-order derivation remain under-specified.
